references.title: Do Industries Explain Momentum?
references.read_scope: Author-affiliated research summary and indexed publisher abstract; full journal text not read.
references.finding: Industry return persistence explains an important part of intermediate-horizon momentum in the studied sample.
references.use: Industry rotation motivation; not a validation of this within-sector high-beta long-only proxy.

references.title: Predicting Stock Returns Using Industry-Relative Firm Characteristics
references.read_scope: Author-affiliated working-paper summary and indexed SSRN abstract; no full-text replication.
references.finding: Distinguishing within-industry firm characteristics from industry averages can improve prediction; intermediate-horizon within-industry momentum is distinct from industry momentum.
references.use: Motivation for subtracting peer return; exact high-beta, liquidity, position count and timing rules are our choices.

references.title: Residual Momentum
references.read_scope: Accepted manuscript abstract and introduction, including discussion of factor exposures.
references.finding: Factor-model residual rankings can reduce time-varying common-factor exposures in the studied long-short portfolios.
references.use: Fama-French residual momentum is a separate hypothesis from subtracting a broad sector mean. We did not implement or claim to reproduce it.

references.title: Momentum crashes
references.read_scope: August 2014 NBER working version: abstract, introduction and section 2.1/portfolio construction; final publication metadata verified separately.
references.finding: Large long-short momentum losses can occur during rebounds after market declines, driven especially by the short loser leg and changing beta.
references.use: Estimate exposures only with past data. This mechanism is not identical to a high-beta long-only basket drawdown.

references.title: Detail for Monthly Momentum Factor (Mom)
references.read_scope: Official construction and stock eligibility notes.
references.finding: The monthly factor uses prior 2–12 returns and monthly formation.
references.use: Supplies the one-month-skip lookback convention. Our equal-weight long-only high-beta portfolio is not the published size-sorted long-short factor.

references.title: Industry classification, industry momentum and short-term reversal
references.read_scope: Indexed publisher abstract only; full text not available in this review.
references.finding: Industry classification and evolving market structure affect industry-momentum results.
references.use: Treat archived broad-sector membership as a proxy and explicitly withhold historical SIC-industry replication claims.

references.title: Explaining and Predicting Momentum Performance Shifts Across Time and Sectors
references.read_scope: Publisher full HTML abstract/introduction and beginning of section 3; not all tables independently reproduced.
references.finding: NASDAQ-sector momentum rankings and performance vary across economic subperiods in the study, including a later evaluation period.
references.use: Modern evidence is related, not a test of our within-sector beta-filtered signal. Do not import retrospective regime labels or horizon selection as live signals.

references.title: Momentum has its moments
references.read_scope: Author-university abstract and metadata only; full methods deferred for a separate risk study.
references.finding: Managing time-varying momentum risk improves risk-adjusted performance in the studied portfolios.
references.use: Candidate basis for a separately registered risk-budget experiment, not a promise that scaling this proxy will improve win rate or eliminate crashes.
